title: Learning failure probability
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose its deterministic decision-tree size is at most $n^d$ for some nonnegative integer $d$. For every $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$, the probability that the program using the decision-tree-size influence bound outputs a hypothesis whose relative Hamming distance from $f$ is greater than $\varepsilon$ is at most $1/10$.
